title: Applications: Diet & BMI
welcome_lead: Apply nutrition and BMI maths to make smart performance choices.
meta_desc: GCSE PE Health & Fitness applications: balanced diet, macronutrients, BMI calculations.
final_note: Awesome — you can now link nutrition to performance with confidence.

concepts.def: Right amounts of carbs, fats, proteins, vits, minerals, water, fibre.
Main energy source for exercise — 55-60% of diet.
Builds and repairs muscle — about 15-20% of diet.
Energy and insulation — about 25-30% of diet.
Maintaining body fluid for temperature and performance.

walkthroughs.body_html: A balanced diet contains carbohydrates (energy), proteins (growth and repair), fats (energy and insulation), vitamins, minerals, fibre (digestion) and water. Athletes increase carbs before competition for energy stores.

BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height² (m²). A 70 kg person who is 1.75 m tall: BMI = 70 ÷ (1.75 × 1.75) = 70 ÷ 3.0625 ≈ 22.9. Healthy range 18.5-24.9. BMI doesn't account for muscle mass, so it overestimates body fat in athletes.

Dehydration reduces blood volume, raises heart rate, impairs decision-making and overheats the body. Athletes should drink before, during and after exercise. Even 2% body water loss noticeably harms performance.
